# Continual-ARC task family notes (task-a130a2b4)

Learned from 2 demonstrations and a solved test instance. Recurring ARC pattern: a uniform background with several solid, axis-aligned monochrome rectangles. Each rectangle may have sparse corrupted cells (including cells replaced by background), and unrelated singleton noise pixels/colors occur outside the rectangles. Output restores each rectangle as a solid rectangle in its original color, and resets all off-rectangle noise to the background color. Infer rectangle extents/color from visible majority/interior evidence; don't preserve stray markers. There may be multiple rectangle colors in a single grid.

- Demo 1: background 1; color-6 rectangles at rows 2–5 cols 3–7, rows 7–13 cols 1–6, rows 17–21 cols 2–5, and rows 24–26 cols 6–8 (0-based); sparse intrusions/holes were repaired and outside noise reset to 1.
- Demo 2: background 5; color-4 rectangles rows 2–3 cols 4–5 and rows 3–8 cols 11–14; color-2 rectangle rows 3–9 cols 25–27. Noise and damaged cells repaired; outside speckles reset to 5.
- Solved test: background 0; rectangle fields in colors 8 and 1 were reconstructed, including noisy/missing cells; external speckles discarded. Correct answer was accepted after several attempts.

Practical approach: identify candidate rectangular patches using repeated same-color cells, treat other colors/background within their bounding boxes as corruption if the patch is strongly supported, preserve every supported rectangle, and replace all isolated noise elsewhere with the dominant background. Don't assume there is only one foreground color.
